title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
summary:
In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative.
With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites.
SpaceX has described its Starmind project as a way to “capture solar energy in space to power” AI capabilities on Earth.
Google has already taken its first steps toward putting compute into space, with the launch of a “Project Suncatcher” AI server satellite last month.
Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin will carry out the first dedicated heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher in 2029.

If you tell Gemini to “read my last message,” it'll speak it out for you and give you the opportunity to reply.
You can also specify the app, otherwise Google Messages will be used by default—Google Chat and WhatsApp are among the others that are supported.

summary:

The Ear Note buds can record your calls, while their charging case can record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations.
Like the Ear 3, the Ear Note’s microphone-equipped case comes with a “Talk” button that you can use to record your own voice.
There’s also a new “Record” button that can record and transcribe your conversations.

title: $799 Smart Glasses Promise Vision Pro-Style Controls in a 45g Frame
summary:
Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams.
The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery.
Savage highlights the bulky hardware currently required for Apple's spatial computing experience, although Orrorin offers substantially fewer capabilities.
Orrorin lacks positional tracking and spatial mapping, so it cannot anchor virtual windows in a room like Vision Pro.
Orrorin is the first product from Savage Technology, co-founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, and remains in engineering validation for now.

title: Location-Accurate Weather For Your Gecko
summary:

[Fraxinas] has taken this a step further though, by making a terrarium that simulates the weather conditions of a gecko’s native New Caledonia.
These are used to simulate the New Caledonian climate, based on real climate data from the island.
On a sad note, the gecko for whom it was built is no longer with us, and after several months of emptiness the terrarium gained a new inhabitant.
This may be the first gecko we’ve seen whose climate follows their real habitat, but it’s not the first automated terrarium we’ve seen.

title: US approves SpaceX plan to send a million data satellites to space
summary:
US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind.
The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, would "support America's booming super intelligence economy".
There is increasing opposition to data centres on earth, including in the US where experts say they were a factor in the Republicans big losses in the midterm elections.
SpaceX believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities".

title: What Australia’s ‘Digital Duty of Care’ Law Means for Big Tech
summary:
Under the Digital Duty of Care law, platforms must provide risk assessments to regulators at least once a year, and they must notify regulators before they introduce significant changes to their platforms that could allow for new risks of harm, such as “addictive” design features.
The amendments also make it easier for Australian citizens to hold tech companies to account.
Previously, one needed to rely on complex legal avenues concerning company negligence and consumer protection.
The new law grants Australians the “private right of action,” which means they can directly sue digital platforms for breaching their duty of care.
